status_summary: On 2026-01-21 HHS OCR signed a notice, published 2026-01-26, disavowing three November 2021 letters that had withdrawn March 2020 religious exemptions for foster care agencies in Michigan, Texas and South Carolina and telling covered entities not to rely on them; the notice does not expressly reinstate the 2020 exemptions. The grant provision remains in HHS's grants regulation: the eCFR for 2 CFR part 300 (current as of 2026-10-01) still contains section 300.300(c), which since 2024 reads HHS sex discrimination statutes to include sexual orientation and gender identity and states that it is interpretive and imposes no substantive obligations outside the Department; the OCR notice describes the 2024 grants rule as having dropped the earlier 45 CFR 75.300 civil rights requirements. An OMB proposed rule of 2026-05-29 on federal financial assistance states it would end sponsorship of gender ideology through funding, but its HHS part 300 text was not readable. No Child Welfare Provider Inclusion Act bill in the 119th Congress was found.

title: Repeal HHS grant SOGI nondiscrimination conditions; faith-based adoption waivers; CWPIA
uncertainties: The OCR notice, the eCFR part 300 page and the OMB proposed rule were read during review. The 2016 condition at 45 CFR 75.300(c) was moved by a 2024 rule (89 FR 80061) to 2 CFR 300.300(c), which now reads listed sex discrimination statutes to cover sexual orientation and gender identity, states it is interpretive, and is paired with a religious exemption notification process at 300.300(d); whether this counts as the same condition the Mandate targets is a judgment. A Federal Register API search found no HHS notice of nonenforcement of 300.300 or 75.300 since 2025-01-20 other than the OCR notice. The OMB proposed rule lists HHS for 2 CFR part 300 under RIN 0991-AC35, but the HHS discussion and amendatory text were not in the page text read, so whether HHS proposes to change 300.300(c) is unknown. The HHS Grants Policy Statement revisions of 2025 were not reviewed. The Child Welfare Provider Inclusion Act was introduced in the 118th Congress; no 119th Congress version was found in one web search, a Federal Register API search and the sources read, but congress.gov was not available. Restoration of exemptions in general is tracked in c14-09. The OCR notice states that a 2024 grants rule dropped the 45 CFR 75.300 civil rights policy requirements, while the eCFR for 2 CFR 300.300 (current as of 2026-10-01) still carries paragraph (c) as interpretive text and paragraph (d) as an exemption notice process; the two fit together if the notice refers to the move of part 75 into part 300 with the condition recast as interpretive text, and the record treats the interpretive successor text as the provision the Mandate targets. The OMB proposed rule was read in the Federal Register web text and the govinfo PDF excerpt; both, and the raw text and XML copies read on 2026-10-18, were cut off before the HHS part 300 text (pages 32198 and 32203 only list HHS and the gender ideology aim). Bill numbers for the 118th Congress were confirmed in GovInfo BILLSTATUS: S. 3344 (introduced 2023-11-27, referred to Finance) and H.R. 6485 (introduced 2023-11-28, last action 2024-12-17); no 119th Congress version was found in one further web search, and the 119th BILLSTATUS file could not be located without a bill number.
